title: 2am hunches — candidate notes: Noor Farid
content:
Context:
Candidate: Noor Farid — onsite loop for Sr. Runtime Engineer (inference serving). Came in via referral; has ~6y infra + ML infra experience, last at small infra startup.

Quick impression (gut, 2am):
- Smart, pattern-y thinker. Not flashy but solid engineering instincts.
- Strong in operational tradeoffs (cost/latency), good at tracing root-cause rather than chasing symptoms.
- Some gaps around large-model attention/kv-codec nitty-gritty; likely learnable but might need ramp time on our custom kernel/quantization work.

Interview notes (panel fragments + my reflections):
1) Systems design (30m)
- Asked to design a model fallback system for degraded capacity (regional outage + GPU OOM surge).
- Proposed multi-tier routing: fast path to high-QPS optimized cluster, slow path to cheaper quantized variants, then fallback to batching-based throttles.
- Liked: emphasis on observable invariants (p95 tail latencies per token, cache-hit metrics, model-compat mismatch counters).
- Missing: concrete on KV cache invalidation logic when model variant changes (how to avoid using corrupted KV across quantization differences). I probed; candidate suggested versioned cache keys but didn't dig into stale prefix problems.

2) Debugging spike (live exercise, 20m)
- Given a trace: high tail latency when sequence length > 1024 despite autoscaling. Candidate walked through likely causes: kernel selection mismatch, batching strategy failing for long sequences (head-of-line blocking), contention on GPU memcpy.
- Proposed quick checks: token-length heatmap, per-gpu memory allocator metrics, dmesg for OOM logs.
- Proposed mitigation: preferentially route long-seq traffic to larger-seq specialized nodes and preempt low-priority batches. Clear, pragmatic.

3) Coding (30m)
- Short exercise to implement a simple LRU prefix cache API (in Python-esque pseudocode).
- Implementation correct-ish: handled put/get/evict, thread-safety via coarse lock.
- Missed an optimization: bulk-eviction/TTL handling and a teardown for async flush-to-disk.
- Overall code clarity good; tests minimal but passed basic cases.

Behavioral / org fit:
- Communicates calmly under pressure, asks clarifying Qs early.
- Mentoring vibe: gave examples of onboarding juniors and pairing on PagerDuty runbooks.
- Concern: previous org was small — will they thrive in a tighter SLA-driven environment? They signaled strong desire to upskill.

Red/Yellow/Green flags (for discussion):
- Green: operational debugging, practical mitigations, observability-first mindset.
- Yellow: limited exposure to quantization/FP16 kernel tuning and custom CUDA kernels. Could be ramped with neighbor pairing and applied-ml mentorship.
- Yellow: preference for coarse locks in high-concurrency code (we prefer lock-free or sharded state for hot paths).

Suggested follow-ups / take-home:
- Small take-home: iterate on the LRU cache to support asynchronous prefetch + versioned keys; include a short plan for cache migration across model variants (3–4 hr). This will test both systems thinking and incremental design.
- Pairing session: 1–2 hour pairing with a senior kernel/runtime engineer to see approach to performance optimization (no pass/fail; more to assess learning curve).

Scorecard (rough):
- Technical: 7/10 (strong infra, weaker on low-level model kernel expertise)
- System design: 8/10 (practical and measurable designs)
- Coding: 7/10 (clear, a few missing edge cases/optimization)
- Communication/Leadership: 8/10 (calm, good mentor signals)
- Overall hire likelihood (my POV): "green-yellow" — lean hire if take-home + pairing are okay.

Open questions I still want answered (for hiring committee):
- Has Noor shipped any quantization/low-bit inference optimizations in production? concrete metrics?
- How comfortable with custom allocator patterns / lock-free queues? Any code references?
- Examples of owning an outage top-to-bottom (timeline + mitigations + postmortem).

Action items (my notes):
- Send take-home prompt by EOD tomorrow (Hannah).
- Ask Arielle to schedule pairing with Marcus (kernel lead) next week if candidate accepts.
- If take-home OK, recommend fast-track to offer conversation (comp and landing zone TBD).

Random 2am hunches (intuition-based):
- Noor will be an immediate contributor to runbook/observability improvements — good bootstrapping for Dedicated customers.
- Might be slightly conservative around risky HPC hacks (fine given our safety bar) — could slow down ultra-low-latency experiments but increase reliability.

Notes to self on framing the feedback in the panel: be explicit about ramp plan and training (applied-ml pairing + kernel internship), highlight observability and ops wins, surface the quantization gap as "ramp risk" not disqualifying.

End.
